ai.description: The Travancore tortoise reaches 23–33 cm. Its carapace is yellowish-brown with dark blotches and a flattened top. Key features include a yellow head and a single gular scute extending forward.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Travancore tortoise is best distinguished by the presence of one or more enlarged, shield-like scales (tubercles) on the side of its forelimbs, absent in other species.
ai.habitat: The Travancore tortoise inhabits evergreen and moist deciduous forests of the Western Ghats, typically found at elevations between 450 and 850 meters.
ai.behavior: The Travancore tortoise is primarily crepuscular, emerging during dawn and dusk to forage for grasses, fallen fruits, and occasionally small invertebrates or carrion.
ai.reproductionNotes: The Travancore tortoise is oviparous, typically laying a clutch of 1–5 eggs in a shallow nest. Breeding occurs between November and January during the dry season.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Travancore tortoise is endemic to the Western Ghats of India, primarily occurring in Kerala, Karnataka, and Tamil Nadu at elevations between 450 and 850 meters.
